name: Isolated Congenital Aglossia

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of the tongue confirmed by clinical examination
Absence of other craniofacial or systemic malformations
Impaired oral functions including feeding and speech due to absent tongue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete congenital absence of the tongue without other associated malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging may assist in excluding other anomalies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete congenital absence of the tongue
Severe ankyloglossia with absent tongue musculature
searchTerms: severe tongue tethering with missing muscles
restricted tongue movement due to muscle absence

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties in neonates due to absent tongue
searchTerms: feeding problems in newborns due to no tongue
difficulty sucking and swallowing as infant
neonatal feeding issues from tongue absence

common.symptomName: Drooling due to impaired oral control

searchTerms: misaligned teeth due to missing tongue

occasional.symptomName: Compensatory hypertrophy of floor of mouth muscles

searchTerms: one side of face slightly different

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to impaired airway protection
searchTerms: breathing difficulty due to airway blockage
shortness of breath from airway protection issues

rare.symptomName: Secondary oral infections due to impaired clearance
Psychosocial difficulties related to speech impairment

imaging: MRI or CT demonstrating absence of tongue musculature
Radiographic exclusion of associated craniofacial anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing absent tongue and oral cavity anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Facial nerve palsy with limited eye movement
Tongue present but may be hypoplastic
Tongue hypoplasia or partial absence rather than complete aglossia

redFlags: Complete absence of tongue causing severe feeding difficulties
Respiratory distress due to impaired airway protection
Failure to thrive secondary to oral dysfunction
references: Smith RJH, et al. Congenital absence of the tongue: clinical features and management. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2018.
Jones MC. Craniofacial anomalies and congenital tongue disorders. Clin Dysmorphol. 2020.
